title: Contrast for CT and MRI: kidneys, allergy, breastfeeding
what: Contrast is a medicine given into a vein so the blood vessels and organs show up better on CT or MRI. For CT it is usually iodine-based, for MRI it is gadolinium-based.
why: When the doctor needs to see organs, tumors, inflammation, or blood vessels better.
duration: the injection takes a minute, and the kidneys usually clear the contrast within a day
tell_doctor: If you ever had a reaction to contrast
If you have asthma or a severe allergy
If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis
If you have diabetes and take sugar-lowering pills
If you might be pregnant or are breastfeeding
If you have thyroid disease, for CT

prepare.title: Test
prepare.text: A blood test for creatinine is often requested to check the kidneys.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked not to eat for 2 to 4 hours. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Unless your doctor limited it, drink plain water the day before and the day of the scan.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If you take diabetes pills, your doctor will say what to do.

bring: Papers about a past reaction to contrast, if any
steps: Before the scan, you are asked about allergies and your kidneys
A thin line is placed in a vein in your arm
During the pictures, the contrast is given through the line
After the scan you are asked to sit for 15 to 30 minutes
feel: For CT: warmth through the body, a metallic taste, a feeling of needing the toilet
For MRI: usually nothing, or a cool feeling in the arm
These feelings pass within a minute
after: Drink more water that day, unless your doctor limited it
Breastfeeding after contrast is usually fine, but check with your doctor
With kidney disease, your doctor may order a test after the scan
red_flags: A rash, itching, swelling of the face or lips, or trouble breathing: call emergency services
Severe pain, swelling, or redness at the injection site
Much less urine in the next days

faq.a: Usually yes, very little gets into the milk. If you are unsure, talk to your doctor.

faq.q: What if I had an allergy to contrast?
faq.a: Be sure to tell the staff beforehand. The doctor will decide whether to change the scan or give medicine first.

faq.q: Is contrast harmful for the kidneys?
faq.a: For healthy kidneys the risk is very small. With kidney disease, your doctor will weigh the benefit and risk beforehand.

reminders.text: Scan with contrast tomorrow. Bring your creatinine test, and drink water unless your doctor limited it.
